Bert Clayton won the Hants County 10 mile walk Championship on January 29th at Eastleigh, in 85m. 45s.; with Percy Wright 4th in 90m. 49s.

However, Bert Clayton sprung a great surprise by leading all the way through and eventually winning the individual race, and although the rest of the team walked exceedingly well, they had to be content with second place to Surrey W.C.
Our "A" Team were second in the scratch race with Harry Churcher, Bob McMullen, Bert East and Bert Clayton scoring 31 points to Highgate Harriers' 23.

Backed up by Bert East, Bob Readman and Bert Clayton, we once again succeeded in winning the scratch team race. The race marked the return of Jack Rutland to racing after a long break, and although he was fairly well down the field, it was pleasing to see him out once again.

Right from the outset, Bert Clayton forged to the front and at 1 mile had a clear lead of 100 yards from the rest of the field, which came along in two batches, the first consisting of probables and possibles, and the second batch of hopefuls and, we hope, future probables and possibles.

Bert Clayton, maintaining his form in our Club 20, led throughout and won easily. Although Jack Rutland moved up quickly around 8 miles from 4th to 2nd place, he later lost some ground, whilst Percy Wright came through to finish 2nd with Jack 4th and Alan Robins 9th.
At the start, Allen got away very fast with Bert Clayton close on his heels and the rest of our boys well up filling various positions from George Oliver 15 to Tony Bellchamber 60.

At 22 miles Bert Clayton started to take a bashing, but with the help of Joe Coleman he picked up really well and there was no holding him. He walked in really grand to finish third and we should all congratulate him on his fine performance.

Mick Porter finished 5th in the Doncaster to Sheffield Marathon Race on Easter Monday, which was run in very bad weather conditions. Bert Clayton was 3rd in the Inter-Counties 7 Miles Track Championship.

At half distance we had a four point lead, with the “ A ” team scoring: Jack Rutland 2, Jack Bidgood 4, Jack Wakeley 9, Bert Clayton was close behind but was having an off day owing to a badly bruised heel.

Our only non-starter was Bert Clayton who has een having some foot trouble and without Bert our chances were not quite so rosy. However this did not deter the others who all got going in nice fashion.
Syd James was well up, with McMullen, Bob Readman and Bert Clayton constituted our team. Gerald Warr had a battle with Gordon Waddingham and George Oliver.

This year we managed to send a team for this race with the result that we scored first three places with Harry Churcher, Percy Wright, and Bert Clayton, with Gordon Waddingham making the fourth in ninth position.

At the start Bert Clayton and Percy Wright got away fairly quickly and at two miles led by about 50 yards. Eight miles was reached by Clayton in 70.36, closely followed by McGreechan, Wright and Checkley; 350 yards behind came Bidgood, Bellchambers, Shields and Rutland, and a further 200 yards Wakel…
Allen, Paddy Woods and our Bert Clayton with a disputed first place; Bert looked very comfortable and seemed quite willing to let the other two set the pace.

Bert Clayton, our first man home, was never further back than fifth place. By finishing second he put up his best performance in this championship, and must have staked his claim for Olympic consideration for 1952.

Only four of our walkers journeyed to Birmingham for this annual event, but what we lost in team honours was compensated for in Bert Clayton's excellent performance in winning the individual scratch race.

The same three also took first handicap team prizes, whilst our " B " team were third; added to this, Bert Clayton was third in the individual handicap, as well as winning the individual scratch race.

With the exception of Bert Clayton, who was previously a doubtful starter, all our " A " Team turned up at Westminster on the morning of September 8th, plus a very plucky " B " Team, who hoped to gain nothing more than a few blisters, and everything looked fairly well set for us to bring the shield back once gain.

On August 18th Bert Clayton was 2nd in the Old Basing 2 miles Open Handicap. Congratulations to Alan Sexton on his brilliant running in Rome for British Services in International Events and more recently his successes in Cambridge University Freshmen's Sports.

Our first casualty was Bert Clayton who is still suffering from knee trouble and was hoping for a hot day. The cold rain soon affected his leg and after two miles he was obliged to drop back, and although making a valiant effort to keep in the race, was eventually forced to retire.
We regret to report that, owing to knee trouble, Bert Clayton is obliged to retire from active walking. In his letter, Bert shows his great appreciation of his fellow Belgravians.

… all the way from Bath with our men, Jack Stirling-Wakely who walked about 65 miles with Fred Herring, Percy Wright and Bert Clayton who were willing helpers during the night in the wilds of Wiltshire, Frank Elson with his wife and daughter who arrived at the half-way mark at 3.30 a.m. and continued…
It is with sincere regret that we record the passing of Bert Clayton at the early age of 39 years; and our heartfelt sympathy is extended to his Wife and three children.
In the early stages, Jack Bidgood Bert Clayton, Jack Baker, Jack Wakeley and George Oliver, walked in a group with Don Heath and Joe Wilson not far away.
Bert Clayton, our new member resident at Eastleigh, gave another good display of walking in finishing eleventh. He will undoubtedly prove a great asset when he qualifies for our teams.
